recentItems.title: Former British MP George Galloway visits Gugulethu Police Station in Cape Town
recentItems.description:
Former British MP and member of the Workers Party, George Galloway is visiting Gugulethu Police Station in Cape Town on what he calls a sentimental journey to reconnect with a police holding cell where he was allegedly detained and tortured 40 years ago by apartheid security forces. 

Galloway a broadcaster and political commentator and British politician and journalist, Yvonne Ridley are in South Africa for a People's Power speaking tour in support of the Palestine people struggles. 

They are being hosted by the Palestine Solidarity Campaign. He's expected to address a Jumuah gathering at the Gatesville Mosque later this afternoon and join a Pro- Palestine Rally at Sea Point on Saturday. #SABCNews #SouthAfrica #sabcnewsonline #fyp #ANC

recentItems.title: DA in Knysna has reacted to the arrest of two senior municipal officials
recentItems.description:
The DA in Knysna has reacted to the arrest of two senior municipal officials and a former councillor. The three were nabbed on Thursday by the police's Political Killings Task Team on allegations of corruption involving a municipal security contract.

 It is alleged that a businessman was asked for kickbacks to ensure the continuation of his contract. The suspects are expected to appear in the Knysna Magistrate’s Court on Monday. 

The arrests come amid ongoing political tensions at the municipality.  DA Mayoral candidate, Levael Davis says they've been raising concerns about alleged corruption and irregular appointments as the opposition.

recentItems.title: Retired Justice Madlanga awarded honorary doctorate by Fort Hare
recentItems.description:
The University of Fort Hare is honouring retired Constitutional Court Justice Mbuyiseli Madlanga with an honorary Doctor of Laws, Honoris Causa. 

The honorary degree recognises Justice Madlanga's outstanding contribution to constitutionalism, human rights and the law, both in South Africa and internationally.

The honour comes just weeks after Fort Hare launched an international moot court competition bearing his name, bringing him back to an institution long intertwined with his journey.
